body: Thinking a little more about this, I realize that the problem may not actually be with the `get_coords_for_body_rid` func per se, as I initially thought from my very limited knowledge of godot, but perhaps with the way the collisions (for the body_rids) are being detected for TilemapLayer on 4.5.dev, because on 4.4.1 it shows that is colliding with 4 different body_rid (4 coords print outputs) whereas on 4.5.dev it only shows 1 console print output.

This is expected. In 4.5, cells are merged together in a single body per quadrant. That means the function is returning the origin of the qundrant now.

Consequently, you can either change the quadrant size to 1 to get the old behavior back. Or you can maybe use the collision point instead. I'd like to implement a helper for that but it's not a simple problem.

In any case, I guess that's a documentation issue.

I just ran into this myself, and I suspect that this change will impact many tile map-based projects, which may be surprised by the change as it breaks backward compatibility in a minor version.

It makes sense why the change was made, and I applaud the performance gains, but I also think that, as it currently stands, it will result in friction and confusion for developers. It kind of goes against the Principle of Least Astonishment.

Essentially, `TileMapLayer.get_coords_for_body_rid()` is the defining way to determine the coords/cell and get to the TileData for collisions, but it isn't appropriately named anymore. In the context of tile maps, "`coords`" is consistently referred to as what could also be called the "`cell_id`". However, `get_coords_for_body_rid()` now effectively returns the "physics quadrant ID".

When defining tiles with dimensions/collisions larger than the TileSet's tile size, you cannot math your way from a collision point to the correct cell within the physics quadrant either. That's a situation where `get_coords_for_body_rid()` was the only proper way to get correct results.

In my opinion, developers would be less caught off guard if the transition is smoothed out a bit, so that projects don't break after an upgrade to Godot 4.5.

A few thoughts:

One option may be to default the `TileMapLayer.physics_quadrant_size` to `1`, so existing projects continue to behave as expected. New projects can tune the setting for improved performance, with the caveat that the behavior of `get_coords_for_body_rid()` has changed.

Another option is to introduce a new `TileMapLayer.get_physics_quadrant_for_body_rid()` method and deprecate the current `TileMapLayer.get_coords_for_body_rid()` method. Perhaps using the old method should print a warning and recommend using the new method instead. Functionally, they would be identical, with the new method just using more semantically consistent language. The deprecation warning then also calls out the behavior change a bit more explicitly.

Using the collision point to calculate the cell within a quadrant sounds good, but as you hinted, it's not simple. The collision point is available for PhysicsBody2D collisions, ray/shape casts, and queries. However, Area2D overlaps, for example, don't include collision points. The `area_shape_entered` signal includes the `area_rid`, which can be used with `TileMapLayer.get_coords_for_body_rid` to resolve the cell.

Given the popularity of Godot, especially in the context of 2D games, I'm somewhat concerned with the level of pushback from the community. Any projects (top-down RPGs, side-scrolling platformers, brick breakers) that use tile maps with custom data layers and/or irregular collision shapes for tiles need that method to look up the cell/TileData/custom data. They'll be forced to either set the `physics_quadrant_size` to 1, or perform additional math, if a collision point is even available, which only works if the collision shape is within the tile's dimensions.

Given that Godot tends to pride itself on being approachable for beginners, but also caters to advanced developers that need more optimized, but perhaps more complex features, I'd vote for the `physics_quadrant_size` to default to 1. The functionality behaves as expected for beginners, doesn't break backward compatibility, and advanced developers have a new option they can tune for their performance needs, with the caveat that it may require additional techniques to resolve collisions to coordinates in some cases.

> One option may be to default the TileMapLayer.physics_quadrant_size to 1, so existing projects continue to behave as expected. New projects can tune the setting for improved performance, with the caveat that the behavior of get_coords_for_body_rid() has changed.

I thought about that, but I decided not to go that route. The choice was between:
- You get bad performance by default
- You got the old `get_coords_for_body_rid` behavior by default.

I decided to go for the first item as `get_coords_for_body_rid` is likely not used that often, and it likely wasn't worth impacting everyone's default performances for keeping a behavior as it used to be (that means all newly created TileMapLayer would have to be slow by default, even in new projects, which I don't think was worth). I understand it caused a small compatibility issue, but I think it's easier to communicate about how to solve this problem for who's updating their project than asking everyone to change their quadrant size every time they instantiate a new TileMapLayer (I wish we had a way to detect old vs new TileMapLayers to select the best default in each case, but I don't think we do right now).

To finish, I also understand why anyone would disagree, I just had to take a decision at some point.

So is there a way to get the cell coordinates of a collision if quadrant sizes > 1 are involved? I guess this is both a question and a potential missing feature with the chunking logic, which is why I'm posting it here.

I currently can't make use of this new feature because there are several places I need to know the tile coordinates a collision happened at to interact with the tiles (it's a platformer with breakable blocks). So unless I'm missing something, I'm effectively stuck at quadrant size = 1 for now.
